title: Abstracts or full text? Evaluating input scope and computational efficiency in biomedical lay summarization
abstract: arXiv:2610.21690v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Biomedical research articles are mainly written for experts and often contain terms that are difficult for the general public to understand. Automated lay summarization has become a solution to make biomedical knowledge easier for patients and the public to understand. However, generating lay summaries from full-text articles requires more computing power because the articles are long and costly to process. Fine-tuning large language models for this task also requires substantial resources. This study asks two questions: (1) whether abstracts contain enough information to produce lay summaries as good as those based on full-text articles, and (2) whether few-shot learning performs as well as task-specific fine-tuning. The study used two public biomedical lay summarization datasets and two recent models, evaluated for readability, factual consistency, semantic similarity, and runtime efficiency. translated_abstract: 生物医学研究论文主要面向专家撰写，通常包含普通公众难以理解的术语。自动化科普摘要生成已成为让患者和公众更容易理解生物医学知识的一种解决方案。然而，基于全文文章生成交互式摘要需要更多计算能力，因为文章篇幅长、处理成本高；为该任务微调大语言模型同样需要大量资源。本研究提出两个问题：（1）摘要是否包含足够的信息，能够生成与基于全文的科普摘要质量相当的摘要；（2）少样本学习的效果是否能与针对任务微调的模型相当。该研究使用了两个公开的生物医学科普摘要数据集和两个近期模型，从可读性、事实一致性、语义相似度和运行效率等方面进行评估。结果显示，基于摘要的摘要生成……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究针对生物医学科普摘要生成任务，系统评估了输入范围（摘要对比全文）与学习方式（少样本学习对比任务微调）在摘要质量与计算效率上的差异，以探索降低计算成本的可行方案。
en_tdlr: This study systematically evaluates input scope (abstracts vs. full text) and learning paradigms (few-shot vs. task-specific fine-tuning) for biomedical lay summarization in terms of summary quality and computational efficiency, aiming to identify cost-effective approaches for generating lay summaries.
